result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. A new supplier defaults to 30, and the terms can be set at registration and changed later. The full offline suite passes (`mvn -q -o test`, no failing surefire reports).

What changed:

- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier` gets `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30`, with a check that it is not negative.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new `paymentTermsDays` component. I kept the old five-argument constructor as a secondary constructor that defaults to 30. That leaves the demo and existing call sites unchanged.
- **`DataStore.java`**:
  - `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the terms.
  - The listings by name, by country and by minimum rating, and `findSupplierById`, read them.
  - I also added them to the other queries that build `Supplier` objects (purchase suggestions, purchased quantity per supplier, supplier performance, spending, single-supplier-per-category). Without that, those views would have shown 30 for every supplier.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: two new tests. One covers the 45-day registration renegotiated to 14 days across all four lookups. The other checks the 30-day default.

Nothing is committed.
